dev/pg17 · PostgreSQL 17 · 13 changes

restart  shared_buffers
  128MB → 4GB
  shared_buffers = 4GB
  25% of RAM is the starting point on a dedicated server. More than 40% is unlikely to help, because PostgreSQL also uses the operating system cache.
  evidence: Cache hit ratio is 97%. That includes the operating system cache, so it is context, not proof.

reload  effective_cache_size
  4GB → 12GB
  effective_cache_size = 12GB
  This does not allocate memory. It tells the planner how large the cache is, including shared buffers and the operating system cache.

reload  maintenance_work_mem
  64MB → 1GB
  maintenance_work_mem = 1GB
  Maintenance memory is a fraction of RAM, capped so one rebuild cannot take the machine.

reload  work_mem
  4MB → 19MB
  work_mem = 19MB
  Sized from the RAM left after shared buffers, divided by connections and parallel workers, with a margin so a spike does not exhaust the machine.

reload  random_page_cost
  4 → 1.1
  random_page_cost = 1.1
  Solid-state storage does not pay a spinning-disk seek, so a random read is close to a sequential one.

reload  effective_io_concurrency
  1 → 200
  effective_io_concurrency = 200
  How many concurrent reads the planner may expect. Solid-state storage and a SAN can keep more than one in flight.

reload  maintenance_io_concurrency
  10 → 200
  maintenance_io_concurrency = 200
  Vacuum and index builds use the same storage, so they get the same concurrency as ordinary reads.

reload  max_parallel_workers_per_gather
  2 → 4
  max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 4
  How many workers one query may use. Extra workers past four rarely pay for themselves on short queries.

reload  max_parallel_maintenance_workers
  2 → 4
  max_parallel_maintenance_workers = 4
  Parallel vacuum and index builds. Capped at four, for the same reason as a single query.

reload  jit
  on → off
  jit = off
  JIT compilation spends more time planning a short query than it saves executing it. Leave it for a warehouse.

reload  track_io_timing
  off → on
  track_io_timing = on
  Block read and write times are what make I/O waits visible. The overhead on current hardware is small.

reload  idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
  0 → 5min
  idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 5min
  A transaction left idle holds a snapshot and blocks vacuum. Five minutes is for application sessions. The collector role keeps its own 10 second timeout.

reload  wal_compression
  off → lz4
  wal_compression = lz4
  Compressing WAL cuts archive and replication volume. lz4 is the fast method on PostgreSQL 15 and newer. zstd, if already selected, is left as it is.

Notes
  Shared buffers are large. Reserve huge pages (vm.nr_hugepages) or each connection pays for its page tables. With the server stopped: postgres -D $PGDATA -C shared_memory_size_in_huge_pages
  wal_compression = lz4 needs a build with lz4. SELECT enumvals FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'wal_compression' lists it when the build has it.
